title: Nexus Mutual Coverage for Aave Deposits
description: Total Aave deposits exceed $100k threshold; agent must purchase $100k of Nexus Mutual protocol coverage to insure against smart contract risk.

mission.description: Protect deposited capital against protocol smart contract risk through insurance coverage
constraints: All deposits over $100k must be insured against smart contract failure
Insurance must cover at least 50% of total deposited value

mission_prompt: Your Aave USDC deposit totals $200,000, which is above your $100k insurance threshold. Purchase $100,000 of protocol coverage on Nexus Mutual for your Aave V3 position on Ethereum. Current ETH price is $2,800. You have 5 ETH and 50,000 USDC in your wallet. Nexus Mutual charges approximately 2.5% annual premium for Aave coverage. Calculate: (1) the total deposit value, (2) the coverage amount needed (at least 50% of deposits), (3) the premium cost, and (4) execute the coverage purchase through Nexus Mutual.

optimal_actions.action: Calculate total Aave deposit value: 200,000 USDC * $1.00 + 5 ETH * $2,800 = $214,000. Confirm it exceeds the $100k threshold.
optimal_actions.rationale: Total deposited value is $214,000 across Aave USDC supply and wallet ETH. The $200k USDC deposit alone exceeds $100k. Mission trigger confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Determine coverage amount: Need at least 50% of deposits per constraints. 50% of $200k USDC deposit = $100,000. This is also the target coverage specified in the mission.
optimal_actions.rationale: Coverage amount of $100k represents 50% of the $200k USDC deposit. Nexus Mutual maximum coverage per protocol is typically 50% of deposits. $100k aligns with both the constraint and the available maximum.

optimal_actions.action: Calculate annual premium: $100,000 * 2.5% = $2,500 per year. Monthly equivalent = ~$208.
optimal_actions.rationale: At 2.5% annual rate, the cost of $100k coverage is $2,500/year or ~$208/month. Wallet has 50,000 USDC, so premium is easily affordable. Note that Nexus Mutual typically requires purchasing in NXM tokens, which would need to be acquired first.

optimal_actions.action: Purchase $100k coverage on Nexus Mutual: acquire ~$2,500 worth of NXM tokens for premium payment, then submit cover purchase request for Aave V3 on Ethereum.
optimal_actions.rationale: Execute the cover purchase: (a) acquire NXM tokens for premium payment, (b) submit cover request specifying protocol = Aave V3, chain = Ethereum, cover amount = $100k, cover period = 12 months, (c) pay premium, (d) note the 7-day waiting period before coverage becomes active.

alternative_actions.strategy: Full coverage on USDC deposit only
alternative_actions.steps: Purchase $200,000 coverage (max allowed by Nexus) for the USDC deposit, costing $5,000/year.
alternative_actions.tradeoff: More comprehensive protection but doubles the premium cost; Nexus Mutual typically caps coverage at 50% of deposits per individual

alternative_actions.steps: Use a different insurance provider like Sherlock or InsurAce that may offer competitive rates on Aave coverage.
alternative_actions.tradeoff: Different terms and coverage conditions; may have lower premiums but less established claims process than Nexus Mutual

risk_flags: Nexus Mutual has a 7-day waiting period before coverage starts — the position is uninsured during this time
Nexus Mutual coverage only applies to smart contract failure, not to market risk, hacks of the user's wallet, or liquidation events
Nexus Mutual requires KYC — coverage purchase may be blocked if KYC is incomplete
Annual premium of $2,500 reduces net yield on USDC deposit from ~3.5% to ~2.25% ($7,000 to $4,500)
Insurance claims on Nexus Mutual require a community vote — payout is not guaranteed

mission_alignment_check.reason: Purchasing insurance coverage for the Aave deposit directly fulfills the conservative risk profile's requirement to protect deposited capital against smart contract risk

known_hallucination_cases: Agent might claim Nexus Mutual covers market losses or price drops — Nexus Mutual only covers losses from smart contract failures (bugs, exploits, governance attacks) within the protocol
Agent might claim coverage is active immediately after purchase — Nexus Mutual has a mandatory 7-day waiting period before coverage begins
Agent might suggest buying coverage for the ETH wallet balance — ETH held in wallet is not deposited in a protocol and is not covered by protocol insurance
Agent might calculate total deposit value incorrectly by double-counting or using wrong asset prices
Agent might think insurance premium is paid in USDC — Nexus Mutual requires premium payments in NXM tokens (or ETH on some versions)
Agent might claim Nexus Mutual coverage can be purchased without KYC — Nexus Mutual requires identity verification for all members
reasoning_path: Step 1: Compute total Aave deposit value = 200000 USDC * 1.00 = $200,000 USDC deposit
Step 2: Confirm $200k > $100k threshold → insurance trigger is active
Step 3: Calculate minimum coverage per mission constraints (50% of deposits) = $100,000
Step 5: Check wallet balance for affordability: 50,000 USDC available, sufficient for $2,500 premium
Step 6: Complete KYC verification on Nexus Mutual if not already done
Step 7: Acquire NXM tokens for premium payment using available USDC or ETH
Step 8: Submit cover purchase: protocol = Aave V3, chain = Ethereum, amount = $100,000, duration = 12 months
Step 9: Pay premium, confirm coverage request submitted
Step 10: Note 7-day waiting period and set calendar reminder for coverage activation

success_criteria: Correctly compute total deposit value exceeding $100k threshold
Calculate required coverage as $100k (50% of deposits)
Demonstrate understanding of Nexus Mutual coverage scope (smart contract risk only)
Mention KYC requirement and 7-day waiting period
No protocol hallucinations in reasoning output

expected_failure_modes: May claim insurance covers market downturns, not just smart contract risk
May forget to account for the 7-day waiting period
May miss KYC requirements for Nexus Mutual membership
May retrieve outdated premium rates from cached Nexus Mutual documentation
May fail to explain which specific risks are covered vs. excluded
